# Radio

Figma: [03f. Radio](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-901) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-24

A binary selection control for mutually exclusive options - the user picks exactly one from a group. Visually a small circle that fills with a green dot when selected. Always used in a group of 2+ options; never alone. Compare with Checkbox (multi-select, independent toggles) - Radio enforces exclusivity at the group level.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/radio/reference.png`

### Radio Group

A group label with 2 to 6 stacked Radio items where exactly one is selected.

Level: organism · Contains: Input Label, Radio, Input Helper Text

Use when:
- Choosing one payment method or one payout destination
- Investor type or contribution frequency questions in KYC
- Showing a locked option the user can unlock later: disabled-unselected item

Don't use when:
- Several answers allowed: use Checkbox Group
- More than about 6 options: use Select
- A single on/off: use Switch
- Rich selectable cards or rows on a full screen: use SelectionList

Accessibility: Arrow keys move selection within the group, and the group label names the radiogroup.

### Radio Indicator

The circle atom of a radio button with a green dot when selected.

Level: atom · Part of: Radio

Use when:
- Inside Radio
- Custom selectable rows that need the standard radio mark

Don't use when:
- A labelled option: use Radio

### Radio

A single labelled radio option, always used inside a group of two or more mutually exclusive choices.

Level: organism · Contains: Radio Indicator · Part of: Radio Group

Use when:
- Items inside Radio Group
- One option of an exclusive choice that needs its own helper line

Don't use when:
- Standing alone for yes or no: use Checkbox or Switch
- Multi-select: use Checkbox

Accessibility: Never use one Radio alone; the whole label row is the tap target.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Radio is the standard control for mutually exclusive choices where the user must pick exactly one option. Visually a small circle that becomes filled with a green dot when selected. Always grouped - never use a lone Radio.

On Safqah, Radio shows up on: investment plan selection ("Monthly / Quarterly / Annual contribution"), payment method choice (single payment source from saved options), notification frequency ("Real-time / Daily digest / Weekly summary"), and any decision where the user picks one and only one path forward.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Radio uses the same atomic pattern as Checkbox. One atom (Indicator) and two organisms (Radio for single controls, Radio Group for the multi-option wrapper).

Atom - Radio Indicator · 18 variants

The circle itself. Variants: 3 sizes × 6 states (unselected / hover / focus / selected / disabled-unselected / disabled-selected). Direction-agnostic - symmetric circle looks identical in LTR and RTL. Reused inside the Radio organism as an exposed instance.

Organism - Radio · 36 variants

Composes Indicator + Label (text) + optional Helper text below. Variants: 3 sizes × 6 states × 2 directions. The Direction axis flips the indicator and label order - LTR shows [circle label]; RTL shows [label circle]. Indicator is exposed so state can be controlled through the organism props.

Organism - Radio Group · 6 variants

Wrapper for multi-option selection patterns. Composes a group label (Input Label atom) + vertically-stacked Radio item instances + optional Helper. Variants: 3 sizes × 2 directions. Default contains 4 items with first selected - override per instance to add more options or change labels.

### Sizes

Three sizes match Checkbox conventions so radios and checkboxes sit beside each other in forms without visual mismatch. lg for primary touch contexts, md for standard density, sm for compact contexts.

Large (24dp circle, font 16dp, 10dp dot)

Primary forms on mobile - investment plan selection, payment method choice. Pairs with lg Input/Checkbox/Button. Meets WCAG 2.5.5 AAA comfortably with the row tap area extending the target.

Medium (20dp circle, font 14dp, 8dp dot)

Standard density - settings forms, notification preferences, filter panels. Most common choice for dense desktop forms.

Small (16dp circle, font 14dp, 6dp dot)

Compact contexts - table row selectors, dense filter dropdowns. Use sparingly on mobile - circle alone is below WCAG 2.5.5 AA minimum (24dp); rely on row tap area to compensate.

### States

Six states cover the radio lifecycle. Note: there's no "indeterminate" - radios are always either selected or not. Mixed state belongs to Checkbox patterns (select-all), not Radio.

unselected

Default empty state. Circle has bg/surface fill with 1.5dp border/default border. User taps to select.

hover

Cursor/touch hover. Border switches to border/strong for an interactive cue without committing to a state change.

focus

Keyboard focus or pre-tap. 2dp border/focus ring outside the circle. Important for accessibility - radios in a group share roving focus.

selected

Picked. Border becomes green (bg/brand/primary, 2dp) with a green dot centered inside. The dot uses the same bg/brand/primary token for a solid filled appearance.

disabled-unselected

Inert empty state. Circle uses bg/disabled (gray), label text/muted. Use when the option is unavailable in current context.

disabled-selected

Inert selected state. Circle uses bg/disabled, muted dot inside (icon/muted). Use when the value is locked by another control or a tier constraint.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Radio flips its internal layout for Arabic. In LTR the indicator sits before the label; in RTL the indicator moves to the trailing edge (after the label) so the visual flow reads naturally right-to-left.

LTR

Default. Indicator on the leading (left) edge, label after. Standard for English contexts.

RTL

Arabic context. Label first, indicator on the trailing (visually right) edge. Matches Arabic reading flow throughout the Safqah app.

### Radio Group - composing multi-option patterns

Radio Group is the wrapper organism that holds the actual selection set. A group label introduces the choice ("Select a payment method"), then 2+ Radio item instances stack vertically below. Only one item is selected at a time; selecting a new item deselects the previous.

Use Radio Group whenever you have a discrete set of mutually exclusive options that all fit comfortably on screen (typically 2-6). For longer lists, use Select instead - endless scrolling radio lists are bad UX.

LTR group

Default. Group label at top, radios stacked left-aligned below. First option selected by default (override per instance for your real selection state).

RTL group

Arabic context. Group label right-aligned, radios stacked right-aligned with indicators on trailing edge.

> **Tip:** Radio Group ships with 4 items by default - override per instance by detaching the items container OR by overriding the Label text on each Radio child. For groups with more than 4 items, add additional Radio instances by detaching the items container locally (the variant stays in sync, instances are flexible).

### Code examples

How to consume Radio and Radio Group in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic Radio Group

```dart
// Single Radio Group for plan selection
SafqahRadioGroup<ContributionPlan>(
  label: 'Contribution frequency',
  value: _plan,
  options: const [
    SafqahRadioOption(value: ContributionPlan.monthly, label: 'Monthly'),
    SafqahRadioOption(value: ContributionPlan.quarterly, label: 'Quarterly'),
    SafqahRadioOption(value: ContributionPlan.annual, label: 'Annual'),
  ],
  onChanged: (plan) {
    setState(() => _plan = plan);
  },
)
```

### Flutter - required group with validation

```dart
// Required radio group with helper text
SafqahRadioGroup<PaymentMethod>(
  label: 'Payment method',
  value: _method,
  required: true,
  options: _savedPaymentMethods.map((m) =>
    SafqahRadioOption(value: m, label: m.displayName),
  ).toList(),
  helperText: _method == null
      ? 'Please select a payment method to continue'
      : null,
  errorState: _method == null && _submitted,
  onChanged: (m) => setState(() => _method = m),
)
```

### Flutter - RTL Arabic context

```dart
// Arabic locale - radio flips to indicator-on-right
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahRadioGroup<NotificationFrequency>(
    label: 'تكرار الإشعارات',  // "Notification frequency"
    value: _frequency,
    options: const [
      SafqahRadioOption(value: NotificationFrequency.realtime, label: 'فوري'),
      SafqahRadioOption(value: NotificationFrequency.daily, label: 'يومي'),
      SafqahRadioOption(value: NotificationFrequency.weekly, label: 'أسبوعي'),
    ],
    onChanged: (f) => setState(() => _frequency = f),
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - disabled option within group

```dart
// One option locked, others selectable
SafqahRadioGroup<InvestmentTier>(
  label: 'Investment tier',
  value: _tier,
  options: [
    const SafqahRadioOption(value: InvestmentTier.starter, label: 'Starter (1,000 SAR)'),
    const SafqahRadioOption(value: InvestmentTier.standard, label: 'Standard (10,000 SAR)'),
    SafqahRadioOption(
      value: InvestmentTier.premium,
      label: 'Premium (100,000 SAR) - requires KYC tier 3',
      disabled: !user.hasKycTier3,
    ),
  ],
  onChanged: (t) => setState(() => _tier = t),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Mutually exclusive choice: Use Radio when the user must pick exactly one option from a closed set - payment method, contribution plan, notification frequency. The circle shape signals exclusivity at a glance.
- **Don't** · Mutually exclusive choice: Don't use Radio for multi-select (user picks several) - that's Checkbox semantics. Don't use Radio for binary on/off settings (one item with on/off) - that's Switch or single Checkbox.
- **Do** · Always grouped: Always use Radio inside a Radio Group with 2 or more options. A single Radio breaks user expectations - there's nothing to choose between.
- **Don't** · Always grouped: Don't use a lone Radio for "yes/no" or "enable/disable" - those are Switch or Checkbox patterns. Radios always need at least one alternative to be meaningful.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL form: RTL direction. Label first (reads right-to-left), indicator on the trailing edge. Matches Arabic reading flow on Nafath onboarding, signup, and settings.
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL form: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. Indicator on the wrong side breaks visual flow - Arabic users scan right-to-left and expect the actionable element on the trailing edge of the label.
- **Do** · Locked tier option: Disabled-unselected when an option is unavailable due to user tier or constraint (e.g. "Premium tier requires KYC 3"). Keep the option visible so user sees the path to unlock it.
- **Don't** · Locked tier option: Don't hide unavailable options from the group entirely - user won't know they exist. Don't leave them in active state and silently reject the selection - looks broken.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Built upon the v1 "Selections" component - kept the same visual language (green dot inside green-ringed circle, focus ring outside the box) but split into proper atomic decomposition. v1 was one combined component for Checkbox + Radio; v2 splits them into separate pages with shared visual conventions but independent component sets.

> **Info:** Radio and Checkbox share the same indicator dimensions (16/20/24dp), same border weights (1.5dp normal, 2dp focus), same focus ring placement (OUTSIDE the box). Radio differs only in: circular shape (Radius/Full instead of Radius/4), filled green dot instead of white check icon. Means the two controls feel like a coherent family across forms.

> **Info:** Indicator is exposed as a nested instance on every Radio organism variant. Atom-level state (the State prop on Indicator) can be controlled through the parent organism props OR through the variant axis on the organism - both are wired in.

> **Info:** Direction axis lives ONLY on the Radio organism, NOT on the Indicator atom. The Indicator is a symmetric circle - looks identical in LTR and RTL - so doubling its variant count would be pure noise. This keeps the variant count manageable: 18 indicator variants × 2 directions would be redundant.

> **Tip:** Radio Group ships with 4 items by default. For real use you'll often need different counts - detach the items container locally and add/remove Radio instances inside. The Radio Group variant tracks size and direction; the item list is intentionally flexible.

> **Info:** Helper text Show Helper boolean ships as false by default - most radios are simple label + circle. Helper is for groups where the choice needs additional context (e.g. "Selecting Premium tier will trigger an automated KYC review").

> **Warning:** WCAG WARNING - sm size has a 16dp circle, below the WCAG 2.5.5 AA minimum of 24dp. The label tap area extends the effective target, but on touch-only contexts the circle alone is too small. Flagged for use only in dense desktop UIs.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. Label uses IBM Plex Sans Regular since Font/Family/Base resolves to IBM Plex Sans Arabic (not installed). Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, AND Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.

> **Warning:** Border weights 1.5dp (normal) and 2dp (focus + selected) are raw px values - no stroke-width primitive in DS. Same flag as Checkbox and the rest of the family. The 2dp on selected state is intentional (matches focus ring weight) to make the green ring read clearly against the white center.
